Issued at 1108 AM CST Sun Nov 15 2026

Earlier this morning an upper level trough/low was located over
the Texas Panhandle with ongoing light precipitation occurring 
north of this system where wrap around moisture and lift was 
still occurring across south central Kansas as of 11am CSt. A 
moist boundary layer and upslope southeasterly flow was present 
across southwest Kansas and as a result there was also areas of 
fog and drizzle occurring across all of southwest Kansas. Patchy
dense fog lingers in a few locations near the Oklahoma border
and across extreme southwest Kansas, however the visibility
trends in these locations indicate that visibilities were 
improving. As a result will allow the dense fog advisory to 
expire at noon. Areas of fog however will still be possible 
through the remainder of the day. 

Rain ending this afternoon but foggy conditions will continue 
through early Monday morning. As the upper level trough moves 
southeast across north Texas late today and overnight, an upper 
level ridge will move across the Rockies and out into the West 
Central High Plains. As this occurs the linger light rain across
south central Kansas will end, however light southeast upslope 
flow and lingering boundary layer moisture will once again favor
foggy conditions remaining in place across southwest Kansas this
afternoon and overnight. Latest probability of dense fog 
tonight is lower compared to earlier this morning west of 
highway 83 however the coverage of the fog tonight does extend 
from the Colorado border to highway 183. Latest REFS currently 
has a 30-50% chance for fog reducing visibilities to 1/2mile or 
less, mainly between midnight and 9am. Based on this will not 
issue a dense fog advisory for tonight, however anyone with 
travel plains Monday morning should be prepared for this 
possibility. 

A gradual warming trend through mid week as gusty south winds 
develop. Following the departure of the upper level trough later
tonight, an upper level ridge will begin to build into the 
Central Plains early next week as the next Pacific upper level 
trough starts to move across the Western United States. This 
will result in a period of dry conditions as the unseasonably 
cool air begins to slowly erode. A trough of low pressure along 
the lee of the Rockies early next week will begin to deepen in 
response to the next upper level trough approaching from the 
west. As it does the southerly winds will increase and 850mb 
temperatures will warm. As winds increase the mixing layer will 
also begin to increase Tuesday and Wednesday. This will not only
allow the warmer air just above the surface to mix down to the 
surface but it will also allow some of the stronger winds from a
40 to 45 knot low level jet to also mix down to the surface. 
Based on the latest BUFR soundings wind gusts from the momentum 
transfer it appears that NBM wind forecast towards mid week may 
be a little weak so will be favoring the stronger 75th 
percentile for winds. If this does verify then wind gusts near 
50 mph will be possible in a few location. Also given the 
unseasonably warm 850mb temperatures spreading across western 
Kansas mid week the current forecast warming trend with highs 
climbing in the 60s by Wednesday still look on track.

Rain chances return to southwest Kansas Friday and Saturday. 
Our next, more significant, upper level trough moving southeast 
across the western United States late week is currently forecast
to move out into the Plains Friday into Saturday. Ahead of this
system, enhanced lift will be present as difluent flow spreads 
into across western Kansas. This will result in an area of low 
pressure at the surface deepening over eastern Colorado or the 
Oklahoma panhandle. Southerly flow late week will also allow 
modified Gulf moisture to be transported northward towards 
Kansas based on increasing PWATs. Base on increasing moisture 
and lift along with a cold front crossing western Kansas will 
result in the improving chances for showers and thunderstorms 
(40-50% chance) along and east of this cold front by late 
Friday. This is something we will be monitoring closely given 
the increasing shear and mid level instability along the cold 
front Friday. 44% of the ensemble clusters today were trending 
towards a slower and deeper upper level trough that will be 
crossing the Texas Panhandle and Kansas. If this scenario 
verifies then a few of the storms that may develop along the 
cold front late Friday may be strong or even severe which is why
we will be monitoring this late week system closely.
